newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In the most dramatic restructuring of its 114-year history, Burns, Philp & Co announced at its board meeting yesterday it has shaken up its senior management structure, a move which has resulted in the resignation of managing director Ian Clack and the company's global yeast and bakery operations president John Cowling. Page 1.

Despite some confusion about entitlements, many retail investors leapt at the immediate profit opportunity stemming from Colonial Ltd's CGH.AX debut on the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday with a 27 per cent premium to the issue price. There were almost 4,000 individual trades, many at the maximum retail lot size of 350 and 550 individual shares. Page 23.

Brierley Investments Ltd's offshoot, Australian Consolidated Investments Ltd, is to pocket A$220 million from the float of its Weeks Bass Strait Royalty, which earns 2.5 per cent of the annual profits from the Bass Strait oil and gas fields, and will use the funds to decrease its debts or make further investments. Page 23.

Thanks to a positive production report, which showed solid gains in iron ore, coal, copper and steel for the month of April, and another surge in the copper price, BHP shares rose 34 cents yesterday to A$19.03, a further indication the Big Australian will report a strong profit rise this financial year. Page 24.

Recently listed theatre developer Cinema Plus Ltd's rapid screen rollout continued yesterday when the company, which operates a large screen theatre in Sydney's Darling Harbour and has agreed to build similar theatres in Melbourne and New Zealand, announced it plans to build an IMAX big screen complex in Adelaide as well. Page 25.

Lachlan Resources NL development evaluation general manager Philip Bruce told shareholders at the annual general meeting yesterday a feasibility study by Lachlan on its key Balcooma project had concluded that it cannot yet be mined profitably, saying "the project is economically marginal". Page 28.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Embattled food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co, which had its origins as a South Sea trading company, announced yesterday it is preparing for a major restructuring involving the sale of its A$800 million herb and spice operations in Europe and North America - a move which will be followed by the retirement of managing director Ian Clack. Page 23.

Shareholders in Colonial Ltd, Australia's second life insurer to demutualise and list, received a boost yesterday when shares in the banking and insurance group debuted at a 27 per cent premium to their issue price, closing at A$3.31, 71 cents above the A$2.60 paid by retail investors. Page 23.

According to an authoritative study of Asia-Pacific economies, headed by Australian academics Professor Ross Garnaut and Professor Peter Drysdale, involving China in the global economic system to avoid dangerous competition from the United States is a priority issue for the region. Page 23.

In a move which represents five years' work since Brierley Investments Ltd's 1992 purchase and renaming of the remains of the Holmes 'a Court investment vehicle Bell Resources, the company is offering Australian investors 10-year rights to royalties on Bass Strait oil revenues, helping to push profit for the 12 months to September above the A$270 million mark. Page 25.

In an announcement which resulted in the market pushing the shares of Australia's only dedicated diamond producer seven cents higher to A$2.26, Ashton Mining Ltd has confirmed the discovery of a series of diamond-bearing kimberlite pipes at its Buffalo Hils prospect in Alberta, Canada. Page 25.

Telstra industry services managing director David Stokes-McKeon said yesterday the national carrier's executives remain receptive to an out-of-court settlement to end an ongoing legal wrangle with service providers over billing accuracy and unpaid debts. He said talks could lead to a commercial settlement, and taking legal action is the last resort. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a move which comes after Burns Philp & Co reported a A$24.4 million loss after tax for the three months ending March 31, the company has admitted failure in its A$800 million foray into the international spice market by yesterday announcing plans to sell its United States and European herb and spice operations. Page 25.

After making a stunning debut on the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, the Colonial Group joined the ranks of the ASX's top 50 listed companies, with a market capitalisation of A$1.91 billion. The Group listed at a 27 per cent premium to its retail price and delivered an average paper profit of A$710 to policyholders who took up shares in the banking and insurance group. Page 25.

New Zealand company Brierley Investments hopes to score a A$110 million profit by putting its Weeks Royalty on Bass Strait oil and gas production out to the public for a 10-year period through a tax-effective trust fund specially created to buy the Weeks royalty from Brierley's Australian investment vehicle, Australian Consolidated Investments. Page 25.

According to Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu 's Insurance Directions report, three life insurance companies dominate almost 50 per cent of the Australian life insurance and superannuation market, with AMP, the largest of the three, capturing almost 27 per cent of the new business market last year. Page 27.

Thanks largely to its A$342 million buyback of Westpac Life Insurance Services from the AMP last October, Westpac Financial Services has posted a 115 per cent profit rise for the half-year to March 31. After-tax profit for the six months was A$38 million,up from A$17.8 million in March last year. Page 27.

According to letters sent to the lawyers of Alan Bond and his former Bond Corp lieutenant, Peter Mitchell, the Ministry of Justice said the two would not be eligible for parole on their Bell Resources convictions - Australia's biggest corporate fraud - for at least two years, eight months longer than Bond and Mitchell had expected. Page 27.
THE AGE

In a surprise move which will see Burns Philp & Co retreat and concentrate on its yeast operations, the group announced plans yesterday to sell its United States and European herb and spice operations, which it bought between 1992 and 1994. It was also revealed managing director Ian Clack will be leaving the company after the asset sale is completed. Page B1.

As demand for stock was driven up by several institutions buying to boost their perceived under-exposure to Colonial Ltd after the institutional bidding process last week, the group's shareholders benefited from a 27 per cent stag profit as the former mutual made its debut on the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday. Page B1.

In a move which Brierley Investments Ltd Australian general manager Don Conway says was conceived in 1993, the New Zealand company is freeing up A$220 million with a 10-year public float of its Bass Strait oil and gas production royalty. The deal refloats a royalty originally housed in the listed company founded by the late Dr Lewis Weeks, the man who advised BHP to search for oil in the area. Page B1.

According to HSBC Markets' Wages Report, which covers 26 enterprise bargaining agreements that include at least 500 employees, the average wage rise in the quarter to March 31 for Australian workers who negotiated their own pay was likely to be too high for the Reserve Bank's comfort. Page B1.

Prompted to make a statement after the Australian Stock Exchange asked why its shares rose as much as 15 cents to A$2.19 on Friday, Western Australian producer Ashton Mining warned yesterday its profit in the half-year to June 30 would be lower than for the previous corresponding period because of the drop in diamond sales since it left the De Beers marketing cartel. Page B3.

In a letter to the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday, base metals giant MIM Holdings announced plans to sell part of its transport division - the Universal Transport Operations businesses in Melbourne, Sydney, Newcastle, Adelaide, Alice Springs, Darwin and Rockhampton, and its freight forwarding arm in Gladstone. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
